So what I'm going to do is explain to you what most Christians believe about the religion. This is called the orthodox or canonical perspective. Christianity has many different factions, but they all believe in a certain interpretation of the Bible.

The core of the Bible is the story of the covenant between God and humans. Covenant means contract or understanding. Throughout the Bible, there are several covenants. The first covenant is between Adam and God. In the Garden of Eden, God says to Adam and Eve, "This is paradise; you don't have to work. Just enjoy life. The food is free and plentiful. Every day, you'll be happy and free of want. You will live forever, but there's only one thing that you must not do: do not eat from the tree of knowledge of good and evil." Of course, Adam and Eve eat the fruit, and God banishes them from the Garden of Eden.

Now society develops as humans work to grow food for themselves. God sees humans fighting and says, "I don't want this; I'm going to destroy everyone and start over." But he likes Noah and tells him to build an ark because God will flood the world. After the flood, God makes a covenant with Noah: never again will he destroy the world.

God still sees humans as wicked and evil and says he needs to find a man who is good to grow a nation that can be a light of the world. He finds Abraham, the father of Israel. The third covenant is when God says to Abraham, "You and your children are loyal to me; I see you as the chosen people, and I gave you the promised land." Over time, Abraham's people go to Egypt where they become slaves. God appoints Moses to free the Israelites from Egypt and take them back to the promised land.

When Moses does this, God says, "Now, what you must do is give the Israelites my law, the Ten Commandments." The law ensures their behavior. Now the Israelites are in the promised land but still worship false gods. God punishes them and finally finds David, who becomes king of the Israelites. God makes a covenant with David: he will always favor Israel as the chosen nation, and the house of David will rule Israel forever.
